Great notes — thanks Ellen. Quick answers and updates inline: 

- Data residency: we can pin telemetry to us-west-2 for the canary. We'll provide a short ingress/egress map and the retention window we propose (30 days sampling, full retention as per contract).

- Cache isolation statement: see below for a standard blurb you can share with Rajiv and I'll also add to the checklist doc: 

  "Redwood isolates per-customer KV/prefix caches per deployment. During canaries we run an isolated routing bucket (dedicated model variant) so no cross-tenant cache contamination occurs; cache warmup uses only traffic labeled for the canary and is not backfilled from production."

- Alert noise policy (canary-specific):
  * Initial tuning: alerts use evaluation-harness statistical significance (we use bootstrap sampling across the prompt set) and require at least two consecutive alerting windows (15m windows) before paging the on-call.
  * Severity levels: P1 = service-level regression (auto-fallback to previous model), P2 = quality regression (notify CS/SE), P3 = informational.

Updated canary/rollback matrix (draft):
- Auto-fallback (immediate rollback): any P1 trigger OR sustained latency degradation >2x baseline for 15m
- Manual rollback w/ CS sign-off: P2 triggers that persist >60m after tuning
- Continue but monitor: isolated P3 signals or single-window noise

Implementation timeline (two-week view):
- Week A: access + prompt sync + eval harness run (dry) + security exchange
- Week B: shadow baseline + 10% canary (Nov 17–18) + post-canary evaluation + final ramp plan

I've uploaded a short guide and the prompt template to the shared Drive link. I'm also attaching qmon-prompt-template.jsonl — Marissa will coordinate the eval-harness mapping.

Laura

Quick technical notes from the implementation side:

1) Prompt format and eval harness mapping\- We'll accept the JSONL prompt set (instruction / input / expected) format you sent. For each prompt we store a canonical id, then run the eval harness (pytest-based runner) to compute baseline metrics (accuracy, F1 where applicable, and safety flags).

2) Canary configuration\- Canary traffic will be routed to a dedicated variant (variant-id: acme-canary-v1). We'll enable prefix cache isolation and an initial batching cap to keep latency stable under low qps.

3) Regression detection thresholds (implementation defaults; we'll tune with you):
  * Accuracy drop >= 5% absolute on the eval set => P2 (escalate to CS)
  * Safety hit: any confirmed unsafe output => P1 (auto-fallback)
  * Latency p95 > 1.5x baseline for 30m => P1

4) Alerts and paging\- During the canary we will route alerts to a joint slack channel (you and our on-call). We'll mute lower severity alerts during the first 2 hours while we stabilize baselines.

I'll prepare the eval-harness runbook and drop it in the Drive folder by EOD today. If everyone is aligned I can schedule the initial baseline run for Nov 10 (dry) and the canary for Nov 17–18.

—Marissa
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
